questions.q: What does this lesson mean by using MITRE ATT&CK "systematically" for hunting?
options: Working through the matrix tactic by tactic, asking whether each technique has actually been hunted for, instead of picking one at random
Replacing hypothesis-driven hunting entirely with automated scanning
Only using ATT&CK after an incident has already been declared
Running every ATT&CK technique's hunt simultaneously in a single query
questions.explain: Systematic use means working the matrix tactic by tactic to check real coverage, rather than hunting one technique whenever it happens to come to mind.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what does T1021 (Remote Services) represent under the Lateral Movement tactic?
options: A tactic name with no associated technique ID
A Sentinel-specific alert threshold setting
A type of malware signature used only by antivirus vendors
A specific technique — using legitimate remote-access tools like RDP or WinRM to move between compromised hosts
questions.explain: T1021 is a specific, ID-numbered technique under the Lateral Movement tactic, describing abuse of legitimate remote-access tools.

questions.q: What is an ATT&CK coverage heat map actually used for?
options: Tracking only the severity of already-confirmed incidents
Replacing the need to ever write a hunting hypothesis
Generating KQL queries automatically without any analyst input
Visualizing which techniques have been hunted for or have detections, so coverage gaps are visible at a glance
questions.explain: A heat map, often built with MITRE's free ATT&CK Navigator tool, shades matrix cells by hunt or detection coverage so gaps stand out.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does a coverage gap matter beyond just being a record-keeping detail?
options: The gap itself becomes the next hypothesis to form and run through the threat hunting loop
A gap means the technique is impossible to ever detect
A gap automatically triggers a new Sentinel analytics rule with no analyst involvement
Gaps should be ignored unless an auditor specifically asks about them
questions.explain: An unshaded technique on the heat map is exactly the kind of specific, testable hypothesis the hunting loop from Lesson 26 is built to run.

questions.q: How does a hypothesis built from an ATT&CK technique differ from any other hypothesis covered in Lesson 25?
options: It can only be used once and then must be discarded permanently
It doesn't differ in kind — it's still specific and testable, just sourced from a named tactic and technique in a published matrix
It never needs to be tested against real log data
It replaces the need for gathering or analyzing any data
questions.explain: The hypothesis is identical in structure to Lesson 25's — specific and testable — the only difference is where it came from.
